2608.28144.title: The Shape of Power: A Multilingual Framework for Social Power Reasoning in Dialogues
2608.28144.paper_summary: Social power plays a fundamental role in shaping human interaction, yet computational studies of power remain limited to narrow linguistic and cultural settings. Existing datasets further lack the demographic and relational depth needed for robust cross-cultural analysis. To address this gap, we introduce a theoretically grounded framework for studying social power in naturalistic multilingual dialogue through movie screenplays. The framework integrates a schema informed by social science theory, a native speaker annotation pipeline refined through pilot studies, and a custom interface for scalable cross-lingual analysis. Using this framework, we constructed an initial corpus containing 15,836 annotated instances from 100 scenes in French and Egyptian Arabic movies. Our analysis reveals strong agreement on observable demographic and contextual attributes, while socially interpretive aspects, such as power asymmetry and intention alignment, remain more contested, highlighting the complexity of social power across cultures. We evaluated 6 Large Language Models (LLMs) and Multimodal LLMs on cross-cultural social power reasoning, finding persistent gaps between human and model agreement in relational and theory-of-mind reasoning. Our work introduces the first extensible multilingual framework for studying social power in dialogues and provides an initial evaluation setting for studying cross-cultural social reasoning.
2608.28144.paper_summary_zh: 社會權力在塑造人際互動中扮演著基本角色，但對權力的計算研究仍然限於狹隘的語言和文化環境。現有數據集進一步缺乏進行穩健跨文化分析所需的人口統計和關係深度。為了解決這一缺口，我們引入了一個理論基礎的框架，通過電影劇本研究自然多語言對話中的社會權力。該框架整合了一個受社會科學理論啟發的模式、一個通過試點研究精煉的母語者註釋流程，以及一個可擴展的跨語言分析自定義界面。使用這一框架，我們構建了一個初步語料庫，包含來自法語和埃及阿拉伯語電影中100個場景的15,836個註釋實例。我們的分析顯示在可觀察的人口統計和上下文屬性上有強烈的一致性，而社會解釋性方面，如權力不對稱和意圖對齊，則仍然存在更多爭議，突顯了社會權力在不同文化中的複雜性。我們對6個大型語言模型（LLMs）和多模態LLMs在跨文化社會權力推理方面進行了評估，發現人類與模型在關係和心智理論推理上的一致性存在持續差距。我們的工作引入了第一個可擴展的多語言框架，用於研究對話中的社會權力，並提供了一個初步評估設置，以研究跨文化社會推理。
